channel.title: The Reed Flute
channel.description: Sufi stories by lamplight, for the heart that aches toward home. Slow, hour-long nights of Sufi tales — Rumi, Attar, Hafiz, Saadi, Rabia, and the Nasreddin Hodja stories — retold in plain words: longing, love, grief, anger, and forgiveness, softened into something you can carry into sleep.
channel.itunes:author: The Reed Flute

item.title: 1 Hour of Sufi Stories When Peace Feels Far | The Reed Flute | Sleep
item.description:
A quiet hour for the heart that lies awake believing rest is hidden in another city, another face, another life. These twelve Sufi tales move through one long night of seekers, dervishes, kings, fools, rivers, mirrors, and desert roads, all circling the tender ache of searching far for what was already near.
In the spirit of the reed flute, cut from the reed bed and singing of home, each story returns softly to the same secret: the distance was never only outside. The road grows still, the lamp burns low, and the heart begins to hear what had been breathing within it all along.

item.title: 1 Hour of Sufi Stories for a Homesick Soul | The Reed Flute | Sleep
item.description:
A quiet night for the one who has wandered from the life once promised to the heart. In a caravanserai near the road home, the reed flute breathes like something cut from its first garden, and twelve old Sufi tales unfold beside a low lamp.
These stories move softly through shame, forgetfulness, longing, mercy, and return. Each one remembers that the path home does not always begin with strength; sometimes it begins with a scent, a small room, a child’s voice, a recipe, a tear, or a dawn that has been waiting without noise.

item.title: 1 Hour of Sufi Stories for a Waiting Heart | The Reed Flute | Sleep
item.description:
When a question has been sent into the dark and no answer returns, the heart can feel like a reed flute cut from its bed, hollow with listening. This quiet night of Sufi stories follows seekers, saints, fools, prisoners, children, and travelers who learn to wait without hardening.
Each tale rests beside the same small lamp: the unanswered prayer, the delayed sign, the door that does not open when the hand first knocks. Let the stories move slowly, like breath through the ney, until waiting itself becomes softer.

item.title: 1 Hour of Sufi Stories for a Hollow Halo | The Reed Flute | Sleep
item.description:
A quiet night of Sufi teaching tales for the hour when goodness feels strained, prayer feels watched, and the heart wonders whether its holiness has become another veil. These twelve stories move through lamps, mosques, markets, desert roads, and humble doors, following the hidden ache of pride disguised as piety.
Like the reed flute cut from the reed bed, each heart remembers a home beyond being admired, obeyed, or proven right. Let these old tales soften the hollow halo, until devotion becomes less like a crown and more like breath.

item.title: 1 Hour of Sufi Stories When You Feel Unseen | The Reed Flute | Sleep
item.description:
Under a quiet indigo sky, this night of Sufi tales tends the fear of being nobody: the small ache that comes when the world passes by, when no one calls the name, when the heart wonders whether its hidden life matters.
Like the reed flute remembering the reed bed, these stories move through caravanserais, gardens, markets, graves, and dawn roads, listening for the worth that does not need applause. The night gathers Ibrahim, Saadi, Rabia, Rumi, Junayd, Attar, Bayazid, Nasreddin, Hafiz, and Uwais into one slow breath.

item.title: 1 Hour of Sufi Stories When Sorry Never Came | The Reed Flute | Sleep
item.description:
For the night when an apology never arrived, this quiet anthology follows one human ache: the heart that has rehearsed another person’s sorry until dawn, then heard only silence. The stories move like a ney breath through caravanserais, sickrooms, courtyards, prisons, and desert roads, tending the place where anger and longing sit side by side.
Across twelve retold Sufi tales, forgiveness is not hurried, forced, or sweetened beyond truth. It becomes a lamp set down in the dark: not to excuse the wound, but to stop carrying the offender inside the chest. Like the reed flute remembering the reed bed, the heart slowly remembers its first home.

item.title: 1 Hour of Sufi Stories When Anger Visits | The Reed Flute | Sleep
item.description:
A traveler reaches a desert caravanserai after sunset carrying a hard feeling in his chest: anger from a wound, shame from a word, fear from what cannot be controlled. Around one low lamp, twelve Sufi tales are retold as a single night of listening, where the heart learns to stop wrestling the visitor at its door.
In the spirit of the reed flute, cut from the reed bed and still remembering home, these stories let bitterness, sorrow, remorse, and heat become softer in the dark. Nothing is forced away. The ache is heard, and by dawn it has less need to burn.

item.title: 1 Hour of Sufi Stories for a Hungry Heart | The Reed Flute | Sleep
item.description:
In a quiet caravanserai at the edge of the desert, a sleepless merchant lies beside closed ledgers, still feeling the hunger for more that no profit has filled. Through the night, an old reed-flute player answers that unrest with twelve Sufi tales: of kings, dervishes, merchants, fools, birds, bowls, jewels, and cups of water.
The reed flute remembers the reed bed from which it was cut, and the human heart remembers a home deeper than possession. These stories move slowly from lamp to lamp, tending the ache beneath wanting, until dawn finds the heart a little less crowded.

item.title: 1 Hour of Sufi Stories for an Unchosen Loss | The Reed Flute | Sleep
item.description:
Tonight’s hour follows one human situation: lying awake after a loss that was not chosen — a person gone, a home changed, a future closed — and trying not to harden around what happened. Through one quiet night of stories, the reed flute keeps returning to its old ache: the reed was cut from the reed bed, yet its crying became music.
These Sufi tales, retold in plain language from Rumi, Saadi, Attar, Rabia, Junayd, Bayazid, and Nasreddin, move softly through grief’s many rooms: silence after prayer, fear after the ground disappears, borrowed things returning, walls breaking, names loosening, seeds planted for a dawn one may never see, and the small thread of love still left in the hand.

item.title: 1 Hour of Sufi Stories for a Wavering Heart | The Reed Flute | Sleep
item.description:
A quiet one-hour anthology for the night when the next step is hidden: a door closing, a road bending into darkness, a decision that cannot yet show its kindness. These twelve Sufi stories move through palace roofs, desert paths, city lamps, sea wind, and starlit bird-flight, following the ache of the reed flute as it remembers the reed bed.
Here the road is not explained all at once. It is listened to. Ibrahim leaves his palace, Musa walks with Khidr, Bayazid returns tiny ants to their home, Rabia trusts an unseen provision, and Attar’s birds travel toward a king they cannot picture. Each tale is told softly, for sleep, until uncertainty feels less like exile and more like the beginning of return.

item.title: 1 Hour of Sufi Stories for a Guarded Heart | The Reed Flute | Sleep
item.description:
Tonight’s hour follows a sleepless traveler who has been hurt in love and has decided to keep the heart closed, polite, and unreachable. Under a deep indigo sky, an old dervish answers that guarded ache with Sufi stories of reeds, thieves, birds, saints, fools, and broken vessels that became more spacious by being opened.
The reed flute remembers the reed bed because it was cut from it, yet its cry becomes music only when breath enters the hollow place. These stories move slowly through caravanserais, gardens, bazaars, river roads, and lamplit rooms, guiding the heart from self-protection toward a tenderness that can break without becoming bitter.

item.title: 1 Hour of Sufi Stories for a Restless Ego | The Reed Flute | Sleep
item.description:
Tonight’s hour follows a tired seeker who cannot sleep after an argument, still rehearsing the words he should have said, still aching to be right, praised, and seen. Under indigo stars, an old dervish tends that hidden fever with Sufi stories about scholars, kings, birds, fools, saints, and lovers whose pride had to soften before wisdom could enter.
The reed flute cries because it was cut from the reed bed, but its song becomes clear only through emptiness. These stories move slowly by river, bazaar, caravanserai, garden, and lamplit door, guiding the heart away from the need to win every room and back toward the quiet source that sees without applause.

item.title: 1 Hour of Sufi Stories for a Jealous Heart | The Reed Flute | Sleep
item.description:
Tonight’s hour follows one sleepless traveler who has seen the one he loves smile warmly at another, and now carries jealousy like bitter smoke in the chest. Through lesser-told Sufi tales from Rumi, Attar, Saadi, Rabia, Bayazid, Junayd, Hafiz, and Nasreddin, the night shows how love becomes poisoned when the heart mistakes fear for devotion.
The reed flute cries because it remembers the reed bed, yet it does not ask the whole river to belong to it. These stories move slowly under gold lamps and indigo stars, guiding a jealous heart back toward a love that can breathe, trust, and release its grip before sleep.

item.title: 1 Hour of Sufi Stories to Love and Let Go | The Reed Flute | Sleep
item.description:
Tonight’s journey begins at a quiet caravanserai, where one sleepless heart is tired from loving someone too tightly. Through old Sufi stories from Rumi, Attar, Rabia, Saadi, Hafiz, Junayd, Bayazid, and Nasreddin, the night slowly loosens the hand that confuses love with holding.
Like the reed flute cut from the reed bed, every story carries the ache of separation. But under the indigo sky, beside lamps and desert roads, the ache becomes softer: love may be real without becoming a cage, and longing may guide the heart home without demanding possession.
